title: Specialized Comparison of 3-Inch (75mm) Flexible Tubing vs. Other Brands in Drip Irrigation Systems
html:
Why is selecting the appropriate hose critical in tape irrigation?

Drip and tape irrigation systems are the backbone of modern agriculture. Among the various components of these systems, the main hose plays a vital role in transporting water from the pump to the lateral lines. 3-inch 75-millimeter collapsible hose This is one of the most widely used sizes for medium flow rates. However, given the variety of imported and domestic brands, choosing an option that is both technically reliable and durable in Iran's climatic conditions is challenging. In this guide, we compare collapsible hoses not just by brand name, but based on key technical specifications such as rubber material (IPR), the number of metal mesh layers, and UV resistance, enabling farmers to make informed decisions. [If you want a better understanding of your farm's water requirements, you can use the article] Comprehensive guide to agricultural collapsible hoses as well]

Structural analysis of collapsible hoses

Multi-layer structure: from the rubber core to the protective jacket

A 75 mm flexible hose typically features a multi-layer structure designed to maintain hose integrity under pressure. The inner layer is usually made of natural rubber or high-quality rubber compound (IPR) to ensure resistance against chemical fertilizers and mineralized water. The middle layer consists of woven steel mesh; for 75 mm hoses, this typically includes between 10 and 16 layers of mesh, which directly increases burst pressure resistance. The outer layer is a PVC or EPDM coating with UV stabilizer, providing resistance to degradation caused by sunlight. The primary difference between brands lies in the polymer type and the bonding technique used for the layers. Older classic brands often use lighter adhesives, which can lead to delamination after several years, whereas more advanced brands use chemical bonding technology.

Impact of 75 mm diameter on flow velocity and pressure loss

The selection of a 3-inch (75 mm) size is generally considered for systems with a pump discharge flow rate in the range of 80 to 150 liters per minute. If your system's flow rate is lower, using this size may cause unnecessary pressure loss at the farthest points of the farm. Conversely, using a smaller size for high flow rates significantly increases flow velocity, leading to rapid wear of the hose's inner wall and damage from suspended particles. Therefore, matching the hose size to the actual pump system flow rate must be done before purchase. For accurate calculation of the required flow rate, studying the calculation of water requirements per hectare can be useful.

Technical comparison of various flexible hose brands

Review of leading imported brands (such as Netafim and Azud)

European and Israeli brands such as Netafim and Azud have high standards in the production of collapsible tubes. A key feature of these brands is the uniformity of the internal diameter along the entire length of the tube, which ensures even pressure distribution in drip tape. These brands also typically provide transparent guarantees regarding UV resistance. Despite higher prices, their main benefit is the increase in yield efficiency per hectare due to reduced water and energy losses.

Review of domestic and cost-effective brands

Iranian brands have also made significant progress. The main advantage of these brands is on-site repairability and access to spare parts. In terms of technical comparison, newer domestic tubes use better galvanized steel mesh, which increases useful life. The strength of domestic brands lies in sizing flexibility and the ability to order tubes of varying lengths without concerns about sea freight. If you are looking to optimize costs without sacrificing irrigation accuracy, these options are highly attractive. For a better understanding of how brand selection affects cultivation, it is useful to study the onion harvesting and cultivation guide which references irrigation details.

Practical Guide: Purchasing and Installation Tips for 75 mm Flexible Hose

  1. Thickness and Material Inspection: When purchasing, feel the rubber granules of the inner layer. The rubber should be firm and bubble-free. The outer layer should appear visually resistant to fouling.
  2. Pressure Test: Always test the hose in a coiled state at low pressure, followed by operational pressure, before installation to ensure the integrity of internal connections.
  3. Installation in Ripper Strip: 75 mm hoses are generally used as main lines or laterals in fields with crop row spacing of less than 5 m. In large systems, avoid pulling the hose across areas with steep gradients to prevent hydrostatic pressure from causing rupture in downstream sections.
  4. Maintenance During Non-Irrigation Seasons: Always drain the hose to prevent residual water from freezing or causing bacterial growth. Store the hose coiled and shaded.
  5. Comparison with competitor brands: Before making bulk purchases, test samples from two different brands in your short-term laboratory conditions to observe pressure drop in practice.

Ultimately, selecting the correct hose directly affects the engineering lifespan of your drip line. You can refer to the drip line guide for farms to select the appropriate hose based on your soil type.

Frequently Asked Questions (FAQ)

  • Is a 75-millimeter coiled hose suitable for greenhouses?
    Yes, but in smaller greenhouses, a 2.5-inch (65mm) size is usually sufficient. A 75mm hose is useful when you have a central pump and the drip lines operate over longer distances to compensate for pressure drop.
  • Which brand lasts longer?
    Durability is relative. European brands have the advantage in UV resistance, but new Iranian brands with stronger meshes offer good mechanical resistance. The best approach is to choose a brand that provides at least a 3-year written warranty.
  • Can a retractable hose be left in direct sunlight?
    No, not for extended periods. Although the hoses are UV-resistant, continuous exposure to intense sun reduces the rubber's elasticity and leads to fatigue cracks.

In either case, the key to success is matching the pipe size to the pump's actual flow rate and maintaining the system correctly during off-seasons. By considering these technical points, you can enjoy optimal irrigation efficiency and reduced long-term repair costs.
